$comment: What the Express reference implementation claims, and the evidence for every requirement not proven by a conformance case. Checked by apps/playground/test/conformance/report.test.ts; rendered to docs/conformance.md.
title: Express 5 + TypeScript reference implementation
limitations: Backends other than Express 5 are not supported (Phase 10).
MongoDB and Mongoose are in the configuration schema but not implemented; createAuth() refuses them.
The in-memory store loses data on restart and keeps rate limits per process. It is capped at authorization level and is not for production.
Email and password only. No OAuth, social login, MFA or passkeys (optional capabilities, not built).
The mailer is a stub: you must implement createMailer() before production, and the server refuses to start in production without one.
`selfauth add` does not merge into an existing Prisma schema.
Production-profile status is self-assessed from the sign-offs below. No independent security audit has been done.

signoffs.finding: docs/data-retention.md lists what deletion clears, deletes, revokes and keeps, how long, and how to purge it; checked against deleteUser in service.ts and the Prisma schema.
A PostgreSQL test makes the role link fail and asserts no user, credential or role row remains: creation is one transaction.
A test asserts the password verifier runs against a dummy hash when the account does not exist.
login() calls verifyDummy() on the no-user path and has no early return before password verification.
A test asserts the hasher runs when registering an address that already exists.
register() hashes the password before looking the email up, so every path costs the same.
Every route in the generated examples is guarded or sits on protectedRoutes(), which denies unguarded routes; a lint-style test fails on a route with no guard.
The config schema rejects malformed permission names.
The config schema rejects project permissions using the reserved 'auth.' prefix.
The config schema rejects roles that reference undefined permissions.
requirePermission() with an undefined permission throws at route registration.
Role and permission sync is exercised against PostgreSQL and never prunes assignments implicitly.
syncRoles runs from the seed script only; the PostgreSQL store does no sync at startup (the in-memory store is seeded on start because it holds no data).
CT-IDENT-007 asserts the stored verifier is an Argon2id PHC string.
Hashing is @node-rs/argon2 (a maintained Argon2 binding, ADR 0014) with algorithm Argon2id; there is no hand-written implementation.
A test asserts a concurrent lightweight request completes while a hash is computed (the library's async API is used).
The config schema rejects minLength below 8.
No setting or code path expires or rotates passwords; the schema's password block has only length, common-password and hashing keys, and a test rejects an added age key.
Unit tests assert the fragment token is read and stripped; the shared browser spec asserts email-link pages send a no-referrer policy.
createAuth() throws when NODE_ENV is production and cookie.secure is false.
safeRedirect accepts only same-origin paths, rejecting absolute, protocol-relative, backslash and control-character targets, in both frontends.
Unit tests cover hostile targets; the browser spec signs in with hostile ?redirect= values on both frontends.
The security workflow runs gitleaks over the full history on every push and pull request and weekly; the config schema has no secret fields.
selfAuthConfigSchema is strict and defines no key that holds a secret; secrets come from environment variables.
For every generated variant a test asserts .env.example holds placeholders only and .gitignore covers .env.
Tests assert startup fails without a valid SELFAUTH_APP_BASE_URL or a required CSRF secret.
Tests assert CSRF secrets under 32 bytes are refused and tokens signed with the previous secret are still accepted.
The previous secret is verified but never used to sign, so rotation cannot keep an old key alive.
The store interface can only append security events (recordEvent), and no route or service updates or deletes one.
The options that reveal registered emails default to false.
The customization guide describes the revealExistingEmail trade-off.
selfauth doctor warns when revealExistingEmail is enabled.
The deployment guide requires HTTPS and shows the HSTS header; createAuth() refuses an http base URL in production.
Migration tests assert the unique indexes exist on a fresh database.
Migrations are planned, applied and verified on a fresh PostgreSQL schema through native Prisma Migrate.
The application never runs a schema sync (no db push, no auto-migrate) at startup; migrations are applied only by explicit commands.
A test runs generation against a database holding application tables and data and asserts they are untouched.
The clients and the conformance runner branch on error.code; message text is displayed but never matched.
The schema uses strict objects; tests reject unknown top-level and nested keys.
Unknown keys are rejected, so a secret cannot be added to the config file.
No field in the schema carries a secret.
Out-of-range TTLs, lengths and timeouts are rejected, not clamped.
createAuth() rejects a configuration naming a database this adapter does not implement (MongoDB).
The schema rejects an unsupported major specVersion.
